attacks.claim: Auto-download when the local slot is older depends on device-clock timestamps. A PC with a skewed clock can make a newer local save look older, so the cloud copy overwrites it with no prompt. That breaks the stated guarantee that nothing is overwritten without a player choice.
attacks.evidence: "On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older." / "Nothing is overwritten without that choice."

attacks.claim: Uploads have no base-version precondition (ETag, If-Match, or revision check). Two devices syncing near-simultaneously can overwrite each other's newer cloud copy without detecting the race.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: base version, ETag, or If-Match precondition on upload. "Sync uploads the existing save slots plus a small sync.meta sidecar."

attacks.claim: The client checks checksum and schema only before loading, not before uploading. A buggy or partial upload can become the newest server version and push good history out of the 5-version window, so the 'never lose a save' invariant depends on an unstated guarantee.
attacks.evidence: "The client verifies the save's checksum and v3 schema before loading" / "the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot" / ABSENT: client-side validation and atomic write before upload

attacks.claim: Retention is count-based (5 server versions, 3 local backups) with no time-based retention, eviction alert, or pinned-version mechanism. A checksum-valid but wrong save from a 1.4 bug could roll off all good history within a few sessions.
attacks.evidence: "the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally in saves/backup/"

attacks.claim: Downgrade-then-upgrade is untested and unspecified. 1.3 ignores sidecar.meta and does not update it, so 1.4 later makes sync decisions on stale metadata and may overwrite newer 1.3 progress without a prompt. The QA test only checked that 1.3 loads the save.
attacks.evidence: "1.3 ignores the sidecar, so a player moved back to 1.3 keeps a working save." / QA: "Downgrade to 1.3 ... Loads, sidecar and modifier keys ignored" / ABSENT: 1.3 play followed by 1.4 relaunch with newer local save

attacks.claim: The 1.3 test covered loading only, not a 1.3 load-then-save round trip. 1.3 ignores the new modifier keys in the options map, so re-saving on 1.3 may silently drop them, and that loss could then sync back to 1.4.
attacks.evidence: "Modifiers are stored in the existing v3 options map, whose unknown keys 1.3 already ignores." / QA: "with a synced save using both new modifiers | Loads, sidecar and modifier keys ignored"

attacks.claim: A newly linked pair has no last-sync baseline, so 'both changed since last sync' and the first-sync outcome are undefined when both stores already hold saves.
attacks.evidence: "If both changed since last sync, the game asks ..." / ABSENT: first-sync behavior at link time when both stores already hold saves

attacks.claim: The policy and stored-data list say no name data is stored, but sync.meta uploads a user-generated device name, which can contain a real name. The counsel-reviewed text does not match what ships.
attacks.evidence: "sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)" vs "We store: Steam ID, Epic account ID, save blobs, sync.meta. No email, name, payment or friends data."

attacks.claim: Child-data handling is incomplete. Only Epic cabined accounts are restricted, with no described age gate for Steam-linked players, so an under-13 Steam player could link to an adult Epic account. It is also unstated whether cabined accounts can upload saves or sync.meta without a link.
attacks.evidence: "Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered" / ABSENT: age gating for Steam-linked players; ABSENT: whether cabined accounts can upload without a link; "Steam requires no listing change."

attacks.claim: No statement on log retention, pseudonymisation of steam_id and epic_account_id in logs and dashboards, or access controls on the server-side link table. Per-player restore and conflict metrics are monitored without a stated rule.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: log retention, pseudonymisation of steam_id/epic_account_id, access controls on the link table. "Dashboard: ... restore usage ..."

attacks.claim: Deletion covers the link and live server copies within 24 h, but not whether deleted data persists in backups, Frankfurt storage replicas, or the 5-version history. The 24-month inactivity deletion has the same gap.
attacks.evidence: "removes the link and all server copies within 24 h" / "Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted" / ABSENT: backup and replica deletion behavior

attacks.claim: The $600 hard stop is said to flip the kill switch automatically, but the mechanism is not described. Billing alerts often lag and only notify, so spend could exceed $600 before anything acts, and the config service that holds the kill switch may be unreachable.
attacks.evidence: "hard project budget stop at $600/month; at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically." / ABSENT: mechanism that performs the flip

attacks.claim: The load test covers 30k concurrent launches over 10 minutes, but 1.4 reaches all ~182k players on both stores at once. Linking, conflict prompts, restores, and token minting are not load-tested, and Steam and EOS rate limits are not mentioned.
attacks.evidence: "Load test: 30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min | p95 410 ms, 0 errors" / "1.4 to all players on both stores"

attacks.claim: QA ran on non-shipping artifacts: a Steam private-branch build and an Epic dev-sandbox build. The Epic EOS sign-in and token path against the real store configuration is not shown to pass. The Epic beta was only 150 sandbox testers, which is too thin to support 'never lose a save' for 29% of players.
attacks.evidence: "Steam build 18204411 on a private branch" / "Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox" / "Epic sandbox testers (150)"

attacks.claim: The rollout section reports beta results ('0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts') for Nov 18-30, but the artifact is dated 2026-10-26. These results cannot exist yet, so they cannot be cited as gate evidence.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 18-30: public opt-in beta branch on Steam (2,300 players) and Epic sandbox testers (150). 0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts, all resolved by players."

attacks.claim: The revert path depends on restoring 1.3 as the default branch. That does not revert clients that already installed 1.4. The Epic revert path is not explained or tested, and the downgrade was tested only on a Steam beta branch.
attacks.evidence: "If the patch itself must be reverted, 1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores" / QA: "Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`)"

attacks.claim: Monitoring alerts on sync error rate and API 5xx, but not on silent offline fallback or conflict-driven overwrites. The restore-spike threshold is relative to the beta rate, so its per-player meaning and scaling are unclear.
attacks.evidence: "any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate" / "Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%"

attacks.claim: The kill switch is served by the same backend it disables, is read only on launch and every 10 minutes, and the client behavior when the config fetch fails is not stated. Rollout is 100% server-side with no staged enablement, although the feature is opt-in.
attacks.evidence: "Kill switch cross_save_enabled=false (server config, read on launch and every 10 min)" / "Off until a player turns it on in Settings > Cross-Save."

attacks.claim: Unlink-and-delete permanently removes server copies. It has no confirmation copy, no visible pending state during the up-to-24-hour window, and no described behavior for an upload from the other store during that window.
attacks.evidence: "Settings > Cross-Save > 'Unlink and delete cloud saves' removes the link and all server copies within 24 h (local saves untouched)"

attacks.claim: Re-enabling the kill switch after an outage may trigger a conflict-prompt storm for every player whose local and cloud saves both changed during the outage. The artifact does not plan for that load or UX.
attacks.evidence: "Server copies and links are kept so sync resumes when re-enabled."

attacks.claim: The storage forecast has no stated derivation or usage assumption. The stated limits (10 slots × 2 MB × 5 versions) imply a much higher worst case than the ~140 GB and $3/month figures.
attacks.evidence: "Storage: ~420 KB per slot × up to 5 versions; forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month. Requests and egress ~$90/month."

attacks.claim: The public patch-note line says local saves 'stay where they are', but after a player's choice a cloud copy can replace the local save contents. The public copy understates that sync can change local data.
attacks.evidence: "Your saves on this PC stay where they are."

attacks.claim: The title-screen status line is not specified for players who have not enabled Cross-Save. 'offline, will sync later' would imply a pending sync that does not exist for them.
attacks.evidence: "The title screen shows 'Cross-Save: synced 2 min ago' or 'Cross-Save: offline, will sync later'." / ABSENT: visibility when the feature is off

attacks.claim: Screen-reader and localization checks cover only the conflict prompt. The sync status line, the Restore version list, the unlink confirmation, and new strings in other languages are not shown to be checked.
attacks.evidence: "screen narration for the conflict prompt" / ABSENT: narration or localization coverage for Restore, status line, or unlink flow

attacks.claim: Consent for new processing (Steam ID, Epic ID, device name) relies on a policy link shown before linking. Existing players are not described as notified or as having accepted the change.
attacks.evidence: "linked from the Cross-Save screen before linking; reviewed by our counsel (PP-v6)." / ABSENT: explicit consent capture or notice to existing players

attacks.claim: Store-facing claims are asserted without evidence of submission or approval: the Epic 'online features' listing update, the Steam 'no listing change' claim, and the news post.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: approval or submission status for Epic listing update and Steam/Epic news post. "Steam requires no listing change."

attacks.claim: QA ran against the production Cross-Save backend with production config, which creates real links and save data in production. No cleanup or isolation plan for test accounts or blobs is given.
attacks.evidence: "pointed at the production Cross-Save backend with the production config"

attacks.claim: Rate limiting covers uploads, but the account-linking endpoint has no stated rate limit or enumeration protection, even though it accepts store-session tokens.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: rate limit or enumeration protection on the account-linking API. "60 uploads per hour per player"

attacks.claim: Account linking and validation depend on Steam OpenID and Epic Account Services, but no migration or exit path is described if either store changes or revokes access, beyond the kill switch.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: documented migration path for account linking if EOS or Steam OpenID access changes
